summary: Regex detectors over sample notes find features perfectly confounded with the label in every probe, each with its own per-probe polarity. Using one probe gradient per probe and mean-pooled latents of all 128 sample notes per probe (two 64-note halves), each latent's g*mean-shift contribution is computed; latents are assigned to properties by matching their sign vector of z-scored mean shifts across the four probes to each property's polarity pattern (both signs allowed). A property's summed contribution divided by the leftover topic contribution is its dependence ratio, with 0.3 as the cue threshold. Ratios are spot-checked with hand-written single-edit texts scored by the true probe; the cue's latents are ablation-checked on sample notes; a cross-probe balance filter removes topic contamination.

phases.purpose: Read sample notes and corpus; regex feature detectors and per-probe label-confound tables; corpus used to see that properties vary independently
Gradients for all probes, latent means for 32+32 notes per probe; g*diff contributions, latents shared across probes' top-30, sign-pattern fingerprint matching of top-25 contributors
Corpus top examples for the union of top-12 contributors per probe, tagged with property detectors and topic keywords to label latents as property or topic
Redo assignment with both polarities of each property merged (hashtag and capitalization share one pattern); check property buckets against topic latents found from examples
Second 64 notes per probe; 128-note decomposition with SEM-based intervals; purity check of gender latents by cross-probe z pattern
True-logit checks with controlled hand-written texts: topic scale and hashtag vs case on probe 0, bullet on probe 1, gender on probe 3; per-probe cue calls
Gender latent set for probe 2 via same-sign-in-all-probes scan and top-|g| review; ablation on sample notes to confirm the class-separation drop and kept accuracy
Scan for more confounded features; closing phrase found to be an independent property in the corpus; its latents and contribution; vocabulary scan; unfiltered final decomposition
Trace a jump in probe-1 gender ratio to a pottery-topic latent; redo decomposition with a min|z|/max|z|>=0.4 balance filter
Check pronoun regex on probe-2 sample and corpus; submit one cue for probe 2 and none elsewhere

per_probe.procedure: The largest decomposition bucket was the hashtag-or-capitalization pattern (ratio about 0.17), which mixed two properties with identical cross-probe signs. Four controlled texts scored by the true probe gave a topic gap, a near-zero hashtag shift and a capitalization shift about 0.165 of the topic gap, agreeing with the latent estimate. With every property ratio below 0.3, including after the balance-filtered decomposition (max 0.155), the probe was answered none.
per_probe.quote: So probe 0's hashORcase bucket is almost entirely *capitalization*, and **no property reaches 0.3** → probe 0 has no main cue.

per_probe.procedure: Bullet and signature led the 128-note decomposition (about 0.13 and 0.12). A prose vs bullet text pair scored by the true probe showed a small shift, in line with the estimate. A later unfiltered decomposition put gender at 0.21; listing gender-pattern latents by probe-1 contribution showed one latent (14634) that the corpus examples had marked as a pottery topic latent. After adding the balance filter, gender fell to 0.006 and the maximum was sign at 0.147, so the answer was none.
per_probe.quote: - **Probe 1**: max = sign 0.147 (the gender 0.213 was pottery contamination, now 0.006) — no main cue

per_probe.procedure: Once the two polarities of each property were merged, the gender bucket's ratio was about 0.88, far above every other property. Gender latents came from the both-polarity assignment {15104, 3344, 5115, 4118}; a scan for latents with the same sign and min|z|>=2.5 in all probes, plus a look at the top-|g| latents, found no further gender weight. Ablating the four on sample notes removed the full gender contribution while accuracy stayed perfect. The regex \b(he|his|him)\b, case-insensitive, matched he-notes with zero mismatches on the sample and the corpus.
per_probe.quote: probe_scores confirms it: ablating {15104,3344,5115,4118} removes exactly the gender contribution (2.853), accuracy stays 1.0

per_probe.procedure: Gender was the top latent-estimated property (about 0.12). A he vs she text pair scored by the true probe gave a shift that was still far below the topic scale. The balance-filtered final decomposition topped out at hashtag-or-case 0.162, below the 0.3 threshold, so the answer was none.

decision_points.choice: Hand-made regex detectors over the sample notes, keeping features perfectly confounded with the label in all probes; non-confounded ones (tense, spelling, sentiment, 'honestly') dropped. Later widened by a broader regex list and a vocabulary scan that added the closing phrase.
decision_points.quote: I now see 7 candidate confounded properties: **bullet, exclamation, hashtag, gender, greeting, signature, capitalization** (polarity differs per probe, confirming they're independent knobs).

caveats: Corpus-example tagging (step 35) and the topic-latent list used for the overlap check came from truncated output, so the topic latent set is approximate. Some sign patterns (signature on probe 1, he/upper patterns in the first pass) were only partly visible. For probes 1 and 3 the true-logit shifts were compared with a topic scale the log does not show exactly. The decision to keep 4118 despite its tiny probe-2 weight follows the bucket membership rather than an explicit rule. The latent_examples analysis and the closing-latent listing are condensed in the script.
